text_plugin_synopsis: Create floating user interfaces with Dear ImGui
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: The current README.md supports the following languages
p_introduction: The ImGui Plugin brings the [Dear ImGui]({{ dear_imgui_url }}) immediate-mode GUI library to AutoJs6, rendering controls with OpenGL ES inside a transparent floating window. It is a natural fit for lightweight floating interfaces such as debug panels, parameter tuners, and runtime HUDs, and keeps window creation, frame scheduling, touch input, and native resource cleanup in one compact API.
p_usage_mechanism: Once the plugin is enabled in the Plugin Center, scripts use the global `imgui` object directly (registered by AutoJs6, which loads the plugin on the first member call); `plugins.load` is not needed. Requires AutoJs6 6.8.0 or later. When the plugin is newer than AutoJs6, members AutoJs6 does not list yet appear on `imgui` only after the plugin is loaded (on the first use of any `imgui` member); the `ui` argument of render callbacks is always complete
features: Adaptive overlay and full-screen Activity sessions with automatic touch pass-through, collapse/expand, independent floating buttons, alpha/security controls, persistent layouts, and lifecycle events.

`launchPrivileged` provides an explicit production SurfaceFlinger mode through AutoJs6-managed Shizuku/root; authenticated Binder transfers the privileged Surface to the complete existing renderer, while `/dev/input` supplies observational pointer input.
AutoJs6 registers the plugin directly as the global `imgui` object, so no loading step is needed once it is enabled, consistent with official plugins such as pinyin / mediainfo.

Transparent floating windows with configurable size, position, frame rate, and font; drag a blank area to move the window, use two-finger inertial scrolling, and long-press with one finger for a right click.
The `inputText` family is fully connected to the system IME, including composing text, automatic soft-keyboard visibility, and common editing keys.
Windows, tabs, tree nodes, tables, popups, menus, tooltips, and 60+ immediate-mode widgets, including a mobile-style `toggle` switch.
Visual and font system with 11 `Themes`, bulk styles, rounded/bordered/shadowed appearances, a multi-font stack, CJK fallback, and a Material Icons subset.
Managed textures accept file paths, encoded bytes, Android `Bitmap`, and AutoJs6 `Image` objects; `image` / `imageButton` and three DrawList layers cover image display and custom overlay drawing.
Lightweight `imgui.ref(value)` / `{value: x}` references work with every stateful control while the legacy Java-array reference helpers remain fully compatible.
Session-managed `logWindow`, stacked `toast`, Promise dialogs, threshold-colored `statsOverlay`, and selectable CRUD `dataTable` components provide ready-made debugging UI.

Common APIs and constant enums have PascalCase aliases (e.g. `ui.Button`) that keep the plugin's argument style; the alias list and the differences from the upstream C++ signatures are in [ALIASES.md]({{ repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/ALIASES.md).

Engineering support includes complete TypeScript declarations, seven runnable examples, Android rendering instrumentation, a lock-free input queue, verified upstream-update tooling, and CI release automation.
Localized plugin metadata, usage instructions, README, and changelog for ten languages.
install_steps: Download the APK matching your device architecture from [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases); pick the `universal` package when unsure.
Install the APK, open AutoJs6, and confirm on the plugin management page that this plugin is recognized and enabled.
Call `imgui.createWindow(...)` directly in your script; grant AutoJs6 the overlay (floating window) permission on first use.
For `launchPrivileged`, first configure and authorize Root or Shizuku in AutoJs6 as usual. The plugin reuses that host state and privileged mode does not require the overlay permission.
p_install_note: Host requirement: AutoJs6 with versionCode 5935 or later. The plugin ships `arm64-v8a` / `armeabi-v7a` / `x86_64` / `x86` binaries and requires Android 7.0 (API 24) or later plus an OpenGL ES 3.0-capable GPU/driver
p_usage_intro: With the plugin installed and enabled, create mutable references and open a floating window
p_usage_references: Mutable controls accept lightweight references created by `imgui.ref(value)` or plain `{ value: ... }` objects; the legacy `imgui.bool` / `imgui.int` / `imgui.float` / `imgui.string` / `imgui.floats` helpers remain compatible. Focusing `inputText` automatically opens the system IME with composing-text support; pass `ime: false` to disable automatic IME handling. Window sizes and positions are dp: the `width`, `height`, `x` and `y` options, the session fields and the event data, and `fontSize` is dp as well. Coordinates inside a frame are px; convert with `ui.dp()` / `ui.px()`. Event and button callbacks run on the script thread (see [THREADING.md]({{ repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/THREADING.md)), and [MIGRATION-1.12.md]({{ repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/MIGRATION-1.12.md) lists the changes from earlier versions. Drag a blank area to move the window (`movable: false` keeps it fixed); two-finger vertical swipes have configurable inertia (`fling`, `flingFriction`, `flingMinVelocity`, `flingMaxVelocity`), and a one-finger long press emits a right click (`longPressAsRightClick`, `longPressDuration`, `longPressSlop`). When the system font does not cover the required characters, point `fontPath` at a TTF or OTF font file.
p_theme_fonts: Themes and fonts: `setTheme` accepts all 11 `Themes`, while `setStyleProperties` updates `StyleVar` values in bulk; `createWindow` also accepts `theme`, `appearance`, `style`, and `shadow`. Its `fonts` array preloads asset (`asset://...`) or file fonts for `pushFont` / `withFont`. The bundled CJK fallback and icon subset are merged automatically; use `Icons` / `icon(name)` to obtain icon glyphs.
p_textures_draw: Textures and custom drawing: call `createTexture` only after the window session is ready (normally once inside its render callback). The returned object exposes `width`, `height`, and idempotent `dispose()` / `close()`; all remaining textures are released automatically when the session closes. `image` / `imageButton` display textures, while `getWindowDrawList`, `getForegroundDrawList`, and `getBackgroundDrawList` expose common drawing primitives. DrawList coordinates are surface-space pixels. AutoJs6 `images.read(...)` and screenshot `Image` values can be passed directly.
p_session_windows: Window sessions: overlays default to `TouchMode.Auto`, which keeps ImGui root windows interactive while letting blank surface areas reach the app underneath; choose `Touchable` or `Passthrough` for a fixed policy. A session can change alpha/security/touch mode, collapse into a low-FPS mini bubble, create independent draggable `addButtonEx` buttons, follow `AlwaysAutoResize` content, persist layout with `iniPath`, and subscribe through `on` / `once` / `off` or option callbacks. Use `imgui.launch(...)` for a full-screen Surface in the currently resumed AutoJs6 Activity and `launchFloaty(...)` for an explicit overlay. Each script engine owns one native renderer session, but that render callback may create any number of ImGui roots with `begin` / `withWindow`; creating another session closes the previous one. An exception thrown by the render callback or an event callback is printed with its stack by `console.error` (a run of the same error once) and emitted as an `error` event (`error` / `phase` / `frame`); without an `error` listener a render error closes the session (`closeReason` is `render-error`), with one the rest of the frame is skipped and rendering goes on. The `debug: true` option reports usage errors such as `begin` without `end` through `console.warn` and logcat, and shows the Metrics and Debug Log windows. Global methods such as `setTouchable` / `setGlobalAlpha` / `getComponent` act on the current session and throw `imgui.<name>: no active session` without one.
p_high_level_components: High-level components attach to the active session and render after the user callback: `logWindow` provides colored levels, clearing, export callbacks, and auto-scroll; `toast` provides positioned timed notices; `alert` / `confirm` / `singleChoice` / `multiChoice` resolve Promises; `statsOverlay` plots frame time; and `dataTable` provides selection and CRUD. The seven bundled examples (`widget-overview`, `parameter-panel`, `log-hud`, `data-table-demo`, `theme-gallery`, `error-handling`, and `background-task`) are discoverable through `listExamples` / `getExampleSource` and launchable with `runExample`. AutoJs6 6.8 does not yet consume the generic example metadata in its Plugin Center, so launch an example directly with the call below until host support lands
p_api_intro: Common APIs also have PascalCase aliases (e.g. `ui.Button` equals `ui.button`). The aliases keep the plugin's argument style (mutable values through `imgui.ref`, for example) and do not match the upstream C++ signatures one to one; see [ALIASES.md]({{ repo_url }}/blob/master/docs/ALIASES.md) for the list and the differences. Lower camel case methods mirror the Dear ImGui operations of the same name and fall into these groups
api_groups: Session runtime: `launch` / `launchFloaty` / `launchPrivileged` / `TouchMode` / `WindowMode`, `setTouchable` / `setMoreTouch` / `setGlobalAlpha` / `setSecure`, `collapseWindow` / `expandWindow`, `addButtonEx`, `density` / `dp` / `px` unit conversion, session `on` / `once` / `off` plus their per-session forms, the session `error` event that reports callback errors, and the `debug` option that turns on debug mode.

Backend discovery: `getBackendCapabilities` / `BackendStatus` reports availability and production readiness for windows, split touch, the privileged process, direct input, Docking, and Multi-Viewport without performing elevation.

Session and windows: `createWindow` / `closeWindow` / `withWindow` / `withChild` / `setNextWindowPos` / `setNextWindowSize` / `setNextWindowBgAlpha`, plus window state queries such as `isWindowHovered`.
Containers and navigation: `withTabBar` / `withTabItem` / `withTreeNode` / `treeNodeEx` / `collapsingHeader` / the `withTable` table family / `withListBox` / `withCombo` / `selectable`.

Style and layout: `styleColorsDark` / `styleColorsLight` / `styleColorsClassic` / `pushStyleColor` / `pushStyleVar` / `setWindowFontScale` / `withGroup` / `withDisabled` / `withId` / `indent` / `sameLine` / `separator` / `spacing`, plus the cursor and scrolling families.

Textures and drawing: `createTexture` / `destroyTexture` / `image` / `imageButton` / `colorU32`, plus `getWindowDrawList` / `getForegroundDrawList` / `getBackgroundDrawList` with line, rectangle, circle, triangle, text, polyline, Bézier, and image primitives.

Queries and input: state queries such as `isItemClicked` / `isItemHovered` / `isItemActive` / `isItemEdited` / `isMouseDown` / `getMousePos` / `calcTextSize` / `framerate`, active focus via `setKeyboardFocusHere`, and the input primitives `addInputCharacters` / `sendKey` / `addMouseWheel` / `wantTextInput`. Every currently exposed `InputTextFlags` value is passed through to Dear ImGui; callback-dependent flags are intentionally omitted, and `WordWrap` applies only to multiline input.

High-level components and examples: `logWindow` / `toast` / `alert` / `confirm` / `singleChoice` / `multiChoice` / `statsOverlay` / `dataTable`, plus `listExamples` / `getExampleSource` / `runExample`; the same factories are available on each session.

Mutable references: lightweight `imgui.ref` (or a plain `{value: x}` object), plus compatible Java-array helpers `imgui.bool` / `imgui.int` / `imgui.float` / `imgui.string` / `imgui.floats` / `imgui.strings`.

Constants: `BackendStatus` / `Cond` / `WindowFlags` / `ChildFlags` / `InputTextFlags` / `SliderFlags` / `TreeNodeFlags` / `SelectableFlags` / `TabBarFlags` / `TabItemFlags` / `ComboFlags` / `PopupFlags` / `HoveredFlags` / `FocusedFlags` / `ColorEditFlags` / `TableFlags` / `TableColumnFlags` / `TableRowFlags` / `TableBgTarget` / `Col` / `StyleVar` / `Themes` / `Appearance` / `Fonts` / `Icons` / `Dir` / `Key` / `MouseButton` / `ButtonFlags` / `TextureFlags` / `DrawListLayer` / `DrawFlags` / `LogLevel` / `ToastPosition` / `Limits`, matching the Dear ImGui enums or plugin tables of the same names.
limitations: Each script engine supports one native renderer session at a time; create multiple ImGui root windows inside that session when several panels are needed. Creating another overlay or Activity session closes the previous one.
`imgui.launch` requires a currently resumed AutoJs6 Activity; use `launchFloaty` when the script must keep rendering without a foreground host Activity.

Privileged mode is fixed full-display and pointer-only in v1.9: it has no IME/key input, host-layer alpha/security, collapse, companion Android buttons, or live rotation rebuild. Direct input observes without `EVIOCGRAB`, and OEM SurfaceControl/SELinux policy may still reject startup; capability probing never executes `su` or requests a Shizuku grant.
text_release_build: Release build with CRC32 digest filenames
text_verify_build: Verify the native source inventory, JNI declaration parity, unit tests, and ABI split integrity
p_build_params: Build parameters come from `version.properties`; the current minimum SDK is 24 and target SDK is 37
p_resource_layout: `index.js` is the script-engine-side `imgui` module and `ImGuiBridge.cpp` is the JNI bridge to Dear ImGui. `strings.xml` contains localized plugin descriptions and `plugin_instruction.md` contains the usage instructions displayed by the host. README and CHANGELOG files are generated from JSON sources by `.python/generate_markdown.py`; edit the JSON sources instead of the generated files
